headline: Record revenue and loan growth push profit higher
summary_short: East West Bancorp's Q2 2026 net income rose 17% year-over-year to $363.7 million, or $2.63 per diluted share, on record total revenue of $791.1 million, record loans of $59.0 billion, and record deposits of $70.1 billion.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 2% q/q and 11% y/y to $684.7 million on loan and securities growth, while net interest margin held near flat at 3.43% (-6bp q/q, +8bp y/y). Noninterest income hit a record $106.5 million on higher lending and deposit fees, offsetting a pullback in wealth-management fees from Q1's record base. Expenses rose 4% q/q on OREO costs and deposit-insurance assessments, nudging the efficiency ratio to 36.7% from 36.2%. Credit provision fell to $33 million from $36 million, though net charge-offs rose to $27 million (0.19% of average loans) from $12 million. Equity grew 3% q/q to $9.2 billion; CET1 rose to 15.44%. No forward guidance is given in this release.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income grew on loan and securities balance growth funded partly by noninterest-bearing deposit gains; noninterest income hit a record on higher lending, loan-servicing and deposit-related fees.

Higher net interest income and record noninterest income were partly offset by higher noninterest expense (OREO costs, deposit-insurance assessments) and a higher effective tax rate versus the first quarter.
Tracks net income's q/q and y/y gains almost one-for-one, since diluted share count was roughly flat both periods.
Not explained in the release; the balance sheet reports the quarter-end cash position without addressing what drove the increase.

Growth is consistent with retained earnings (+$252.6M, matching net income less roughly $110M of dividends paid) partly offset by a modestly wider AFS-securities unrealized-loss position within accumulated other comprehensive loss.

Record net interest income, revenue, loans and deposits in Q2 2026; management cites 17% tangible-common-equity returns and 14% tangible-book-value growth y/y, with credit quality stable despite a modest uptick in net charge-offs and nonperforming assets.
